hints: Focus on what $\Delta H^\ominus_z$ actually represents, the change from $\text{C(s)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ to $\text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$.
Notice that going via $\text{CH}_4\text{(g)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ uses formation of methane then combustion of methane, so apply Hess's Law around that triangle.
Consider what burning $\text{C(s)}$ and burning $2\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ separately would make, and check whether burning $\text{CO(g)}$ starts from the same elements.
walkthrough:
**Identify the target change**

Think of $\Delta H^\ominus_z$ simply as the direct route at the bottom right of the cycle.

$$\text{C(s)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \quad \Delta H^\ominus_z$$

**Test expression 1 using Hess's Law**

Going from the bottom to the top left is formation of methane, then top left to top right is combustion of methane.

$$\Delta H^\ominus_z = \Delta H^\ominus_f\text{CH}_4\text{(g)} + \Delta H^\ominus_c\text{CH}_4\text{(g)}$$ 
So expression 1 is correct.

**Test expression 2 from combustion definitions**

Recall combustion of carbon and hydrogen make exactly the products we want.

$$\text{C(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$ 
$$2[\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}]$$ 
Adding them gives $\text{C(s)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$. So expression 2 is correct.

**Test expression 3 and conclude**

Combustion of $\text{CO(g)}$ starts from $\text{CO(g)}$, not from $\text{C(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$.

$$\text{CO(g)} + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$ 
This does not match the starting elements for $\Delta H^\ominus_z$, so expression 3 is incorrect. Therefore only 1 and 2 work.

options.A: This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Expressions 1 and 2 are valid by Hess's Law, but 3 is not because $\Delta H^\ominus_c\text{CO(g)}$ forms $\text{CO}_2$ from $\text{CO}$, not from $\text{C(s)}$, so the starting materials do not match $\Delta H^\ominus_z$.
options.B: This option states only 1 and 2 are correct. Expression 1 follows the cycle via methane: formation plus combustion. Expression 2 adds combustion of C and combustion of 2H2 to give exactly $\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Both equal $\Delta H^\ominus_z$.
options.C: This option includes 3 but omits 1. Expression 3 is wrong because it introduces $\text{CO(g)}$ as a reactant, which is not present in $\Delta H^\ominus_z$. Expression 1 is actually correct and should not be omitted.
options.D: This option includes only 1. While expression 1 is correct from the triangle, expression 2 is also correct because $\Delta H^\ominus_c\text{C(s)} + 2\Delta H^\ominus_c\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ sums to the same overall change to $\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
